__meta__.description: keyhole 5090-measured vision corpus, clean ONNX for the three-platform sweep (backend=Orin+5090, qualcomm=iq9 QNN/HTP, same ONNX both sides vs 5090 baseline).
__meta__.baseline_5090: data/output/rtx5090_corpus_trt.json — same ONNX, TensorRT, compute_ms median. Legacy per-model anchors also in data/output/bakeoff/*_summary.json.
__meta__.note: ALL SEVEN are now fully static: batch=1, fixed spatial size, no free shape tensors. Precision is a per-model axis: run FP16/INT8 at minimum; add INT4/MXFP4 where your harness supports it.
revision_2_changes: FIX (rev1 was BROKEN): resnet50v1.onnx stores 101/110 initializers as external data and the 97MB sidecar `resnet50v1.onnx.data` was missing from the rev1 bundle — the graph would not load in onnxruntime. The sidecar is now included and MUST be kept next to the .onnx.

FIX: three models carried dynamic dims despite rev1's 'fixed batch=1' claim. Frozen via scripts/freeze_onnx_static.py — clip_vit_b32_visual image->[1,3,224,224]; efficient_sam_vitt_encoder batched_images->[1,3,1024,1024]; efficient_sam_vitt_decoder image_embeddings->[1,256,64,64], point_coords->[1,1,1,2], point_labels->[1,1,1].

FIX: efficient_sam_vitt_decoder's `orig_im_size` was an INT64 SHAPE TENSOR whose values drive Gather ops. Benchmark harnesses fill unbound inputs with random data, so this was a latent garbage-output/OOM trap on any platform. It is now frozen as a constant initializer [1024,1024].

measurement_protocol.headline_metric: compute_ms median — pure accelerator kernel time, excluding host<->device transfers. This is the apples-to-apples number across a discrete GPU (5090), an integrated SoC (Orin), and an NPU (IQ-9075).
measurement_protocol.also_report: end-to-end latency incl. transfers. Unified-memory parts look better on this; quote both so the difference is visible rather than argued about.
measurement_protocol.warmup: >=3s of untimed inference before the timed window, so DVFS has boosted.
measurement_protocol.int8_caveat: keyhole's INT8 numbers are PERF-ONLY: no calibration cache, arbitrary dynamic ranges (trtexec convention, inputs +/-2.0, layer outputs +/-4.0). Kernel selection and latency are representative; numerics are NOT. Do not compare accuracy against these.
measurement_protocol.partial_delegation: If part of a graph falls back to CPU/GPU, say so and quote END-TO-END. (Per qualcomm's Neutron methodology note — a whole-graph number and a partially-delegated number are not the same measurement.)
